samples.summary: `copyThread` detaches a docs-range anchor with `detachYorkieValue`, which mangles the array-valued `posRange` into CRDT metadata
samples.evidence: `copyThread` does `anchor: (detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) ?? {}) as AnyAnchor` (comment-ops.ts:99) and its doc comment claims this "covers all three anchor shapes". It does not cover the docs one. A `docs-range` anchor's `posRange` is the tuple returned by `tree.pathRangeToPosRange([start,end])` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:166,185) — an ARRAY, stored in the CRDT as a Yorkie array proxy. `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray` (yorkie-json.ts:172), which is false for a Yorkie array proxy; the repo states this itself in yorkie-json.ts:15-20 ("a chart's `seriesColumns` or a slide's `elements` would come back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata") and again in comment-ops.ts:110-124. So on a live document `GET .../comments` on a `doc` returns every thread with `anchor.posRange` replaced by CRDT bookkeeping, and the same broken anchor is echoed by `setResolved`/`reply` (which return `copyThread`). Nothing catches it: the doc fixtures added in this delta (comments.controller.spec.ts:567) and the only anchor-detachment unit test (comment-ops.spec.ts:263-283, PDF `rect`, a plain object) both omit `posRange`. Wrong result on the path the docs half of the feature exists to serve — a consumer cannot resolve or re-anchor the thread it is handed.

samples.summary: `deleteThread` answers 404 instead of deleting when the thread's comment list is empty
samples.evidence: `deleteThread`'s authorize callback computes `rootCommentId(thread)` = `copyThread(thread).comments[0]?.id` (line 614), which is `undefined` for a thread whose `comments` array is empty. `assertCommentAuthor` then takes `const comment = commentId ? findComment(...) : undefined;` and throws `NotFoundException('Comment not found')` (lines 527-528). The thread demonstrably exists — `mutateMap` found it at line 575 — so a thread left with no comments (a partially applied concurrent CRDT edit, or a legacy/imported thread) is permanently undeletable through the API and is reported as a 404 that contradicts the same thread appearing in `GET`. The new flat-root tests only exercise two-comment threads, so nothing covers it.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: comment-ops.ts:99 does detach the thread anchor via detachYorkieValue, whose only array handling is Array.isArray (yorkie-json.ts:172), false for a Yorkie array proxy — a fact this repo documents three separate times (yorkie-json.ts:14-20, yorkie-json.spec.ts:155-162, docs/tasks/archive/2026/08/20260827-v1-worksheet-review-fix-lessons.md:13-23, where it is recorded as a previously-shipped defect producing {createdAt, movedAt}). The docs-range anchor's posRange really is an array (frontend/src/types/comments.ts:31, TreePosStructRange) and really is stored as a Yorkie array (yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-84 says so explicitly; written from tree.pathRangeToPosRange at yorkie-comment-store.ts:166,185). The path is live rather than fixture-only: comments.controller.ts:250-257 lists doc threads from doc.getRoot() of a real attached yorkie.Document (yorkie.service.ts:36-56), and mutateThread returns copyThread (comments.controller.ts:599) for setResolved/reply. No guard exists — copyThread has no docs-range branch, and the sole anchor-detachment test (comment-ops.spec.ts:263-283) uses a plain-object PDF rect with no posRange. Result: GET/PATCH on a doc hands back anchor.posRange as CRDT bookkeeping, so the caller cannot re-anchor or resolve the thread — wrong behavior on a normally-reachable path, major and blocking under the correctness rubric.
